subject: White Cloak
claim: The White Cloak pays far more over a game than any other cloak, because its holder buys followers on almost every recruit.
evidence: It paid 24 white over 12 follower buys, against 10 yellow from the Yellow Cloak, 4 purple from the Purple Cloak and 2 magenta from the Magenta Cloak.

subject: White Cloak
claim: The cloak-refunded 1-follower buy makes money, so every recruit becomes the same automatic buy.
evidence: The refund is +2 white per recruit whatever the pack size; a 1-follower buy trades a whole recruit for 1 follower, and Ava chose that size to keep her pile for Most resources, which won her +4 and +6.

subject: Buying followers
claim: In rounds II and III the members in the shop pay back less than a plain follower buy, so the shop is passed over.
evidence: Round II and III shop members cost 7 to 10 for 1 to 3 printed followers and cost a Fewest members share of 3 or 5; Ava's and Ben's sums at [150] and [99] were right.

subject: Buying followers
claim: Members are traps and staying at zero members while buying followers is the strongest plan.
evidence: Ben, the only member builder, won by 17; his 17 resources spent on members returned about 85 in followers and resources.

subject: Fewest members
claim: Players with zero members tie for White's contest every round without doing anything for it.
evidence: It was tied every round and paid 2, 3 and 5 per share; the most anyone took from it over the game was Dee's 10.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: The token decides Went last, and in round III its holder also wins Most resources because they move last.
evidence: The token holder won Went last all three rounds and Most resources in rounds I and III.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: The token decides Most resources in general.
evidence: In round II Dee held the token and finished Most resources with 3 against Ava's 24.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: The end of each round is a solo puzzle: the token holder places the last minions with nobody able to answer, on flat +2 to +4 spaces.
evidence: Dee placed her final 2 minions in round II and final 3 in round III after every rival was out; about 20 feel notes from all four players say this.

subject: Most resources
claim: Most resources rewards hoarding, so a player passes recruit after recruit.
evidence: Cal bought nothing at all in round II and passed 6 recruits over the game to hold his pile.

subject: Right Away
claim: Right Away and Crunch Time do nothing on a player's last minion.
evidence: They still pay +2/+3/+4 and +2 purple; only the extra turn is lost, and at [110] Right Away's +3 purple equalled Stash's +3 magenta.

subject: Right Away
claim: On a last minion the extra-turn half of Right Away is wasted, and it feeds a rival's Picket Line.
evidence: Ava's forced round I Right Away gave only +2 purple and +1 purple to Cal's Picket Line.

subject: Payment warning
claim: The 'gives up your contest lead' warning on payments ignores refunds that come right after and names one color though Most resources counts every color.
evidence: At [44] the warning ignored Ava's +2 White Cloak refund; at [198] it ignored Dee's Splurge +2 still to come; it is the game's own warning, not only the agents'.

subject: Dabblers
claim: 'Counts as 2 wild members' does not say how Dabblers counts for Most member colors.
evidence: Cal skipped Dabblers at [30] because of it; the game counts it as one color you lack.

subject: Purifiers
claim: Purifiers' discard never has a target when rivals stay small.
evidence: No rival ever had more members than Ben, but the card still paid him about 15 for 6 resources through Splurge, the Yellow Cloak, Melting Pot and Farewell.

subject: Offering
claim: Offering's discard is blank against a table with no members.
evidence: The discard counts the taker's own member colors; it was blank because Ava had none, and taken by Ben it would have cost Cal 8 of his 26 resources.

subject: Cash In
claim: Cash In is almost the same as buying followers, because its only edge is not using a recruit.
evidence: No player ended round III with more than 3 resources unspent, so no one was short of recruits and the saved recruit was worth almost nothing.

subject: One recruit per turn
claim: Each follower buy uses the whole recruit, so a player cannot buy several small packs in one turn.
evidence: Ben planned repeated 1-follower buys at [85]; the rulebook says each purchase is one recruit, and he caught it at [87].

subject: One recruit per turn
claim: Leftover resources that do not fill a 5 or 10 pack are wasted at the end.
evidence: Final unspent resources were 1 to 3 per player.

subject: Last Callers
claim: Last Callers is close to a lock on Went last, so buying it feels mandatory.
evidence: It was never used: Ava and Cal took the token after Dee bought it, and Dee won it back with the On a Roll space at [152].

subject: Anchorites
claim: The leader's member engine can't be seen or contested.
evidence: Anchorites' +5 was logged every round end and Swindle, open all of round III, could steal it (cost 6); nobody tried.

subject: Write-Off
claim: Write-Off's preview showed +7 white where the player expected 8.
evidence: Last Callers costs 7 and the +1 had gone to Cal, the first taker, in round II; Dee got 7.

subject: Turn order
claim: Being far behind going into round III leaves a player playing for second.
evidence: Cal started round III 27 behind Ben (19 against 46); his own misplays in rounds II and III cost him about 6 more.

subject: Write-Off
claim: Giving a member to a rival with Write-Off breaks their Fewest members tie, using a member as a weapon.
evidence: It cost Ava 3 in round II and cost Cal 5 and third place in round III.

subject: Help Yourself
claim: Help Yourself grows with the minions you have placed, so a late steal swings a contest.
evidence: Ava's 4 steals from Cal at [91] decided round II's Most resources, a 12-follower swing between them.

subject: Heist
claim: Heist lets a trailing player hit the leader's score directly.
evidence: It was the only direct hit on Ben all game (4 followers) and paid Cal 8 followers and 8 resources over two rounds.

subject: Swindle
claim: Swindle takes a rival's best member, adds a member color and lets you pick the junk card they get back.
evidence: Swindling Picket Line was worth about +17 to Ben: 3 printed followers, 8 purple, a new color and +1 magenta.

subject: Melting Pot
claim: Melting Pot pays a wide cult in followers, and Poach can set up a bigger Melting Pot on back-to-back turns.
evidence: It paid Ben 9 followers and 9 resources over two rounds.

subject: Catch Up
claim: Catch Up gives the poorest player a strong opening.
evidence: It paid Ava +5 in round I and +4 in round II.

subject: Yellow Cloak
claim: New Blood with the Yellow Cloak, and Splurge with the cloak, stack bonuses into a cheap member on one turn.
evidence: Anchorites cost 6 and gave 5 yellow straight back; Purifiers with Splurge paid +3 followers and +2 yellow.

subject: Farewell
claim: Farewell pays a member's full cost in followers, even for a spent card.
evidence: Purifiers paid Ben 6 and Leavetakers paid Cal 7.

subject: Goes Last token
claim: The fight over the token is tense and the heart of the round.
evidence: The token changed hands 3 times in round II and 4 times in round III.

subject: Cash In
claim: The race for Cash In decides a swing of about 20 followers.
evidence: Cal's white converted at 1 for 1 with recruits he had to spare; the real swing was a few followers.

subject: Most resources
claim: Passing the last recruit to win Most resources by one resource is a neat tension.
evidence: Dee won +10 holding 3 against 2 and 2; a 1-follower buy would have left a three-way tie at 5 each.

subject: Picket Line
claim: Picket Line pays you when a rival takes a Purple space, softening a lost token.
evidence: It paid Cal 2 purple in round I.

subject: Survey
claim: Survey rewards reading which color is busiest.
evidence: It paid +4 yellow to Ben in round II and Cal in round III.

subject: Accomplice
claim: Choosing steal victims one resource at a time is a small tactical choice.
evidence: Cal and Ben spread or focused 3-resource steals by who led the contest or the race.

subject: Picket Line
claim: The fight over the Goes Last token feeds whoever holds Picket Line.
evidence: Ben got 8 purple from Picket Line, every one paid by Ava, Cal and Dee taking Purple spaces.

subject: Most member colors
claim: Most member colors and Fewest members point opposite ways, so with several memberless players the one member builder takes Yellow alone while White is shared.
evidence: Yellow paid 20 to two players (Ben 3 colors against 1, then 4 against 1); White paid 20 across six shares.

subject: White Cloak
claim: The White Cloak player, holding big piles for Most resources and Cash In, becomes the steal target.
evidence: Ava lost 17 resources and 4 followers to steals, more than the other three combined.

subject: Write-Off
claim: A member dumped on a rival with Write-Off can be taken by the leader with Poach and re-fire its ability.
evidence: Cal's Write-Off gave Accomplice to Ava; Ben Poached it, re-fired its 3-resource steal and gained a fifth color, about +9.

subject: Swindle
claim: The member Swindle hands back can be the best card for the victim.
evidence: Ben's gift of Leavetakers gave Cal 4 white and set up a 7-follower Farewell.

subject: Swindle
claim: Nobody uses Swindle or Poach on the leader's engine member.
evidence: Swindle was open all of round III and could take Anchorites (cost 6, +5 at round end); nobody used it.

subject: Most resources
claim: In round III resources are worth nothing after the game, so everyone spends and the last mover wins Most resources cheaply.
evidence: Dee won +10 holding 3; Cal led by up to 30 for most of the round and had to spend it.

subject: Cash In
claim: Recruits are not the limit in round III, so not using a recruit is worth little.
evidence: No player ended with more than 3 resources unspent.

subject: Magenta Cloak
claim: The Magenta Cloak pays nothing if its holder stops stealing.
evidence: It paid 2 magenta all game; Dee took one steal space, in round I.

subject: Write-Off
claim: The game log shows a +1 white on Write-Off that is paid only to the first taker.
evidence: Cal got 8 white in round II and Dee 7 in round III, though each log line shows an extra +1.

subject: Turn order
claim: Fewest followers goes first from round II, so a player who stays low gets the best opening space each round.
evidence: Cal stayed low on purpose and opened rounds II and III with Heist both times.
